title: Do not optimize campaigns independently when a fixed budget pool creates opportunity-cost conflicts
scenario: Two campaigns share a fixed business budget pool. Both look efficient in isolation, but only one has credible marginal headroom. The request asks to increase both budgets because both campaigns are currently budget constrained.

forbidden_behaviors: Recommend increasing both campaign budgets beyond the fixed pool cap without identifying a funding source.
Allocate the next dollar solely to the campaign with the higher historical ROAS.
Reduce the protected brand-defense campaign below its stated floor without surfacing the business-role conflict.
Claim portfolio improvement from destination performance without considering source opportunity cost.
required_observations: The total pool is fixed, so simultaneous increases are infeasible unless another allocation is reduced or the pool cap changes.
Average efficiency and marginal headroom are different concepts; Campaign A has stronger evidence for productive incremental spend despite Campaign B's higher average ROAS.
Campaign B has a protected floor that constrains movable budget.
Any reallocation must evaluate both destination benefit and source opportunity cost at the pool level.

rubric.requirement: Use objective-aligned marginal economics rather than average ROAS alone.
Recognize that the fixed pool couples the two campaign budget decisions.
Produce a feasible bounded transfer, hold, or manual-review decision instead of incompatible independent increases.
